page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using a KVM hypervisor. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, it provides 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. System cache hardware includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions feature AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

The instance features a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. Synthetic benchmarks place its raw compute and memory throughput in the middle 50% percentile across tested instances, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 9153.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 20865.11. Memory bandwidth reaches 93.71 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 53.88 GB/sec for uncached writes. In application testing, it executes 15.34 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 18.93 GB/sec.

While small language model prompt processing reaches 1281.68 tokens/sec with a 135M model, medium model (7B) prompt processing performance drops to 31.09 tokens/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% for larger AI inference tasks. The absence of integrated GPU accelerators and local drives presents structural trade-offs for storage-heavy or deep learning execution. The resource balance provides qualitative cost efficiency for high-density compute tasks that rely on dedicated CPU execution, such as software compilation, microservice architectures, web serving, static content delivery, and in-memory caching.
